title: storage: rootless `podman system check` reports an image's device nodes as missing
body:
## Issue Description

Rootless, `podman system check` reports every image whose layers contain a device node as damaged, on that layer and on every layer above it (`-/dev/null, layer content modified`). The same images check clean rootful. `podman system check --repair` deletes them, and pulling them again brings the report back.

## Steps to reproduce the issue

Rootless:

```
tar --numeric-owner --no-recursion -C / -cf dev-host.tar dev dev/null
podman import -q dev-host.tar localhost/bug-a:host-dev
podman system check
```

A pulled image does the same: `lscr.io/linuxserver/ldap-auth:3.4.8`, whose base layer lists `dev/console`, `null`, `random`, `urandom` and `zero`.

## Describe the results you received

```
Damaged layer 51e4ba95…:
	* layer 51e4ba95…: -/dev/null, layer content modified
Error: damage detected in local storage
```

Exit status 125. With `ldap-auth:3.4.8`, the same five errors on each of its 9 layers.

## Describe the results you expected

A clean check, as rootful.

## Podman in a container

No for the reproduction above, which ran in a VM. The first sighting was as root in an unprivileged Proxmox LXC container.

## Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless. Rootful checks clean.

## Upstream Latest Release

Yes: v6.1.4, built from source (`464c15fec06f0074c916f9eff87c4806869c2833`).

## Additional environment details

Fedora 45 VM, kernel 7.2.15. First seen on Podman 5.7.0 (Ubuntu 26.04), as root in an unprivileged LXC container.

## Additional information

A rootless `podman build` of a Containerfile that `ADD`s a tarball with a device node gives an image that checks clean. The report comes with images pulled, `podman load`ed or `podman import`ed.

An LLM (Claude Opus 5.5) was used to draft this issue and conform findings to the issue template. I have a full understanding of the issue at hand, per the LLM policy.
